story: story-042 — per-client setAsideBuffer added to skimSurplus

criteriaApplied.high: Assets stolen/lost/compromised directly or via valid attack path without hypotheticals.
criteriaApplied.medium: Assets not at direct risk, but protocol function/availability impacted, or value leak with stated assumptions and external requirements.
criteriaApplied.low: State handling, spec deviations, centralization (non-critical discouraged).
criteriaApplied.centralization: Owner/admin privilege bundle — judged by likelihood and reasonable misuse impact.

ledgerLink.kind: amplification — distinct deliverable activated under non-zero aggregate buffer

classification.title: Recipient's effective slippage tolerance amplified by 1/(1-f) under non-zero aggregate buffer, breaching the M-02 bounded-leak premise
classification.assetImpact: Recipient (typically a yield accumulator such as SYA) absorbs the swap's absolute slippage delta over a SMALLER principal slice (toRecipient = underlyingReceived * (1 - f)). Recipient's per-skim fractional leak scales as slippageBps / (1 - f). At f = 0.5 leak doubles; at f = 0.9, 10x; at f = 0.99, 100x. Absolute floor still bounded by per-swap minOut at the AMM level, but the bound the M-02 acceptance memo relied on (slippageBps * tradeSize against recipient principal) is parametrically broken.
attackPath: 1. Owner configures one or more clients with non-trivial setAsideBufferSize via setSetAsideBuffer (in-design operation).
2. The aggregate buffer fraction f = totalBufferShares / totalShares becomes non-zero.
3. Any skimSurplus is executed against a vault NAV that diverges from AMM clearing price (sandwich window, depeg, thin liquidity) — same precondition as M-02.

4. The swap's minOut is computed against pre-buffer aggregate totalShares; the buffered slice is paid first to clients[] without slippage attribution; the recipient receives whatever is left of the slipped output.
5. The recipient's fractional take is reduced by (1-f); the recipient's per-skim leak (as a fraction of recipient yield) is amplified by 1/(1-f) relative to the M-02 bound.
classification.likelihood: medium — requires (a) owner to have configured non-zero buffer (story-042's deliberate feature), (b) the same execution-window conditions that make M-02 exploitable (NAV vs AMM divergence, sandwich window, looser slippageToleranceBps). Conditions (a) and (b) compound multiplicatively — neither alone produces the amplified leak.
assumptions: Buffer fraction f > 0 (i.e. at least one authorized client has setAsideBufferSize > 0).

M-02's underlying NAV-vs-AMM divergence window is exploitable on the configured route (deep sUSDe/USDe pair makes this marginal at f=0; at higher f the same marginal swap becomes economically material for the recipient).
Recipient is treated as the protocol's economic counterparty for the skim (the M-02 acceptance memo's framing).
externalRequirements: AMM pool conditions: depeg or thin-liquidity window that the M-02 acceptance memo already accepted as parametric residual.

classifiedFindings.justification: Medium because (1) no direct asset theft — the swap's absolute minOut at the AMM still bounds the worst-case underlyingReceived; (2) the leak is a VALUE LEAK with STATED ASSUMPTIONS and EXTERNAL REQUIREMENTS (M-02's depeg/divergence window + owner-set non-zero buffer), which is the exact framing C4 Medium specifies; (3) protocol availability is not impacted — skimSurplus still completes. The borderline rationale for keeping this Medium rather than High: although DEDUP-001 BREACHES the parametric bound the author accepted in project_reflax_nav_floor_tradeoff.md (the bound scales as 1/(1-f), not as a fixed slippageBps), the recipient is still curated by the owner (setClient is onlyOwner), the buffer fraction is itself owner-set, and the loss is bounded per-swap by the AMM minOut (which holds against the swap's gross output even if amortization shifts on distribution). The amplification is parametric — not break-glass — and the owner can mitigate by capping slippageToleranceBps (per L-01) and adopting an aggregate buffer cap (per CLASS-002). Promoting to High would require either (a) a no-buffer-configured exploit path (collapses to plain M-02, already acknowledged) or (b) a way for an external attacker to cause toRecipient ≈ 0 without owner cooperation — DEDUP-002 shows the silent zeroing requires owner-set buffer = 100%. Neither pathway is unconditional. Recommend the author re-confirm acceptance under the parametric envelope OR adopt the recipient-anchored minOut mitigation (option c).
promotionTriggers: If author elects to ship setAsideBufferSize defaults at non-trivial fractions (>10%) without an aggregate cap AND keeps slippageToleranceBps uncapped → revisit as High (the combined surface admits sandwich attacks where the recipient bears the entire slipped output).
If a future strategy is deployed against a non-deep ERC4626 where the M-02 acceptance memo's 'sUSDe NAV is not atomically manipulable' premise fails → DEDUP-001 becomes a theft primitive, not a leak.
classifiedFindings.decisionLog: Memory project_reflax_nav_floor_tradeoff.md records the author accepting the bounded-leak premise. DEDUP-001 shows the bound is breachable by an owner-configurable buffer fraction — but the configuration is owner-bound, the per-swap absolute leak is still capped by minOut, and the recipient is owner-curated. Medium is correct under C4's 'value leak with stated assumptions and external requirements' clause. Anchoring rationale: per-swap absolute leak is preserved (HM-bar not crossed); per-recipient fractional leak is parametrically unbounded (justifies promotion above QA/Low).

ledgerLink.kind: operator footgun within centralization envelope; companion to CLASS-001

classification.title: No aggregate cap on per-client buffer percentages allows total set-aside to reach 100% of underlyingReceived, reducing recipient take to zero with no revert
classification.assetImpact: No direct loss — all funds remain protocol-owned (buffered slices go to authorized clients). Recipient and downstream integrators relying on skimSurplus return value receive zero proceeds despite the swap consuming surplus and incurring slippage. Companion enabler for CLASS-001's worst-case parametric leak (f → 1).
attackPath: 1. Owner configures multiple authorized clients with high setAsideBufferSize values whose sum-weighted product reaches or exceeds 100% of underlyingReceived.
2. setSetAsideBuffer accepts each call (only per-client <=100% check) — no aggregate cap revert.
3. On the next skimSurplus, _distributeBuffer transfers totalSetAside == underlyingReceived to clients; toRecipient collapses to 0.
4. The skim completes without revert; SurplusSkimmed event fires with the recipient parameter that now received nothing.
classification.likelihood: low — requires an owner fat-finger or coordinated buffer-set across multiple clients summing to 100%. Owner is trusted; intent to do this would be effectively malicious. Operator footgun framing applies per feedback_revert_over_silent_clamp memory.
assumptions: Owner is benign but may misconfigure (operator/keeper-driven setter calls are a realistic source of malformed input).
externalRequirements: Owner exercises setSetAsideBuffer across enough clients to push the sum-weighted buffer to or near 100%.

classifiedFindings.justification: Low because (1) no asset loss — all funds reach protocol-owned addresses; (2) protocol function (the skim itself) still completes; (3) the defect is a setter-design gap that admits silent misconfiguration. Per feedback_revert_over_silent_clamp.md, this is a valid Low (operator/keeper-driven mis-config that a require/revert would have caught), NOT a dismissible 'admin reckless mistake' OOS finding. The recommendation is to either (a) track an aggregate buffer cap on setSetAsideBuffer with require ceiling or (b) require toRecipient > 0 in _distributeBuffer when buffer is non-zero. C-01 covers the owner-trust envelope; this is the specific setter-design defect within that envelope and merits its own entry per regression-mode policy.

classification.title: setAsideBufferSize persists after a client is deauthorized and silently resurrects on re-auth
classification.assetImpact: No direct loss. Misallocated yield on the post-reauth skim: surplus that should have flowed to the recipient is diverted to the re-authorized client per the stale buffer percent. Magnitude bounded by the size of the next skim and the stale buffer setting.
attackPath: 1. Owner calls setSetAsideBuffer(clientA, 50). Storage: setAsideBufferSize[clientA] = 50.
2. Owner calls setClient(clientA, false). Storage: _authorizedClients removes clientA; setAsideBufferSize[clientA] still equals 50 (never zeroed).
3. Time passes. Owner re-adds clientA via setClient(clientA, true) — perhaps after an address rotation or post-incident re-enable.
4. Next skim: _accrueSurplusShares reads setAsideBufferSize[clientA] = 50 and diverts 50% of clientA's principal-weighted surplus to clientA — even though no fresh setSetAsideBuffer call was made.
classification.likelihood: low-medium — realistic in any deployment that rotates client integrations or temporarily disables a client during an incident. Operator footgun.
assumptions: Operator may toggle client authorization (a designed operational pattern).
Operator does not re-verify all per-client buffer settings after re-auth (a realistic omission).
externalRequirements: setClient(client, false) followed by setClient(client, true) with no intervening setSetAsideBuffer(client, 0).

classifiedFindings.justification: Low because (1) no direct loss — surplus is misallocated between owner-curated parties; (2) the invariant violation (setAsideBufferSize[client] != 0 should imply _authorizedClients.contains(client)) is a concrete state-consistency defect with a documented exploit sketch; (3) recommendation is explicit clear-on-removal or membership guard on setSetAsideBuffer — aligns with feedback_revert_over_silent_clamp.md. C-01 covers the owner-trust envelope; this is the specific resurrection-on-reauth defect.

classification.title: SurplusSkimmed event under-represents the buffered-path beneficiaries — no event records per-client buffer redirection
classification.assetImpact: No direct loss. Downstream integrators (indexers, accounting systems, SYA's reconciliation logic) reading SurplusSkimmed as the authoritative receipt event will mis-attribute proceeds: every wei routed to clients[i] via _distributeBuffer is invisible to the event consumer. Off-chain accounting drift.
attackPath: 1. Buffered-path skim executes; _distributeBuffer performs safeTransfer to each surplus-bearing client.
2. Only one event fires: SurplusSkimmed(token, client, msg.sender, surplus, recipient) from _accrueSurplusShares — naming recipient as the destination.
3. Integrator reconstructing fund flow attributes the entire surplus to recipient; the per-client buffer transfers are missed.
classification.likelihood: high (the integration mis-attribution is automatic on every buffered-path skim once any client has setAsideBufferSize > 0). Severity remains Low because the impact is off-chain accounting only.
assumptions: At least one client has setAsideBufferSize > 0 (buffered path active).
An external integrator relies on SurplusSkimmed for fund-flow reconstruction.
externalRequirements: Any indexer or reconciliation pipeline consuming SurplusSkimmed events.

classifiedFindings.justification: Low because (1) no on-chain asset risk — all funds reach protocol-owned addresses; (2) the event contract is the canonical integration surface and is now incomplete for the buffered path; (3) author CLAUDE.md only documents the sum-vs-return-value drift, not the recipient mismatch. Per feedback_per_repo_audit_scope.md, the submodule owns its event contract — this is a valid submodule-side finding. Spec deviation with concrete observable impact on integration.

foldingCandidate.rationale: Both findings cover the integration-transparency surface of the buffered path (event-recipient drift + return-value-path-dependent semantics). Report-writer/qa-bundler should decide whether to bundle into a single 'buffered-path integration transparency' QA item or keep separate (audiences differ: event indexer vs return-value caller). If both stay QA-tier in the report, recommend bundling.

classification.title: skimSurplus return-value semantics are path-dependent — fast path returns swap output, buffered path returns recipient-receipt; NatSpec leaves room for integrator confusion
classification.assetImpact: No loss today. The contract IS correct (per econ-scanner C5 self-correction: toRecipient is returned on buffered path). Risk is documentation/maintainability: a future refactor that adds a buffer or tax on the fast path would silently change the return-value semantics. SYA-style integrators applying minRewardTokenSupplied against the return value are protected (the buffered-path return is more conservative).
attackPath: 1. Future maintainer refactors the fast path to add a buffer or tax on top of underlyingReceived.
2. NatSpec ambiguity does not flag the semantic change — return value silently shifts from 'swap output' to 'recipient net' on the formerly-fast path.
3. Downstream caller that anchored against 'swap output' silently mis-prices.
classification.likelihood: low — depends on future refactor introducing the inconsistency; integrators are conservatively safe today.
assumptions: Future maintainer extends the fast path without updating the return-value semantic.
externalRequirements: Integrator depends on a specific interpretation of the return value across both paths.

classifiedFindings.justification: Low because (1) no on-chain bug — the contract returns the correct value on both paths today; (2) the concern is documentation/maintainability and integrator clarity; (3) the per-feedback memory feedback_per_repo_audit_scope.md applies — the submodule owns its return-value contract NatSpec. Recommendation is explicit NatSpec clarification (option a in DEDUP-005). Per CLAUDE.md quality standard, this is borderline-foldable into CLASS-004 — both speak to the buffered-path integration transparency surface.

ledgerLink.kind: owner-config footgun within centralization envelope; first-time ledger appearance for unchanged CurveAMMAdapter

classification.title: setRoute accepts tokenIn == tokenOut and paths with internal zero-gap segments — relies entirely on off-chain verification
classification.assetImpact: No direct theft (Curve Router NG enforces minAmountOut at the AMM and the strategy layer applies a NAV-anchored minOut on top). Realistic bad outcome: strategy DoS — deposit/withdraw/skimSurplus revert until the operator corrects setRoute. Availability impact bounded by time-to-fix.
attackPath: 1. Operator (or off-chain deployment script) submits a malformed route to setRoute: e.g. tokenIn == tokenOut, or path = [tokenIn, 0, pool, 0, tokenOut, 0, ...] with an internal zero gap.
2. setRoute's validation passes (only checks path[0] == tokenIn and last non-zero entry == tokenOut).
3. First swap against the malformed route reverts at the Curve router or produces zero output; strategy operations dependent on the route DoS until operator re-runs setRoute with corrected payload.
classification.likelihood: low — depends on off-chain deployment-pipeline error. Per submodule CLAUDE.md, verification is delegated off-chain; per feedback_revert_over_silent_clamp memory, an on-chain require/revert is the correct defense-in-depth.
assumptions: Operator may submit a typo or copy-paste error in route deployment payload.
externalRequirements: Off-chain script or operator submits malformed route via setRoute.

classifiedFindings.justification: Low because (1) no theft path — Curve Router NG's minAmountOut and strategy NAV-anchored minOut both protect against fund loss; (2) realistic bad outcome is self-DoS, recoverable by re-running setRoute; (3) author CLAUDE.md defers verification off-chain — this is a documentation note, NOT an acceptance memo (per project policy, off-chain deferral does not auto-OOS the on-chain defense-in-depth gap); (4) recommendation is require/revert per feedback_revert_over_silent_clamp.md. C-01 covers the owner-trust framing; this is the specific setter-design defect.

upstreamLedgerNotes.L-01-overlap: L-01 is the existing slippage-cap finding (setSlippageTolerance default-0, no upper bound). DEDUP-001 recommendation (a) explicitly cites L-01 as the slippage-cap mitigation; ECON-001's recommendation overlaps the L-01 mitigation surface. No re-classification of L-01 is needed — it remains Low/open. The CLASS-001 (M-04) recommendation should reference L-01 as a partial mitigation but the medium classification stands independently because L-01 alone does not address the (1-f) amplification.
upstreamLedgerNotes.C-01-envelope: CLASS-002, CLASS-003, CLASS-006 all sit within the C-01 owner-power envelope but each is a distinct setter-design defect with concrete blast radius. Per regression-mode policy and feedback_revert_over_silent_clamp.md, these are valid Lows orthogonal to the centralization framing in C-01. C-01 remains a Centralization-class entry covering the owner-trust bundle; new Lows track specific defects.
upstreamLedgerNotes.M-02-acknowledgement: The author's acceptance memo (project_reflax_nav_floor_tradeoff.md) is parametrically broken by CLASS-001 (M-04) under non-zero buffer fraction. The acknowledgement does NOT extend to the (1-f)-amplified leak; CLASS-001 is therefore a new report-worthy deliverable, not a duplicate of M-02.

borderlineCases.reason: Medium vs High judgment call. Kept Medium because per-swap absolute leak is still bounded by minOut at AMM, recipient is owner-curated, and the parametric breach is owner-configurable. See promotionTriggers in the classification block.
borderlineCases.flaggedFor: human review at report-writer stage; reviewer may upgrade to High if (a) deployment ships with non-trivial buffer defaults without aggregate cap, or (b) M-02's deep-pool premise relaxes.

borderlineCases.reason: Borderline-foldable into CLASS-004 at report-writer/qa-bundler stage. Both speak to buffered-path integration transparency.
borderlineCases.flaggedFor: qa-bundler — recommend bundling into a single 'buffered-path integration transparency' QA item if both stay QA-tier in final report.

notes: 1 Medium, 4 Lows, 1 Low (foldable). No Highs surfaced.
CLASS-001 (M-04) is the headline deliverable: a quantified amplification of M-02 that breaches the existing author acceptance memo when any client carries a non-zero buffer.

CLASS-002 / CLASS-003 are the two operator-footgun surfaces that enable CLASS-001 via owner misconfiguration; both are setter-design gaps within the C-01 envelope but with concrete blast radius and require/revert recommendations.
CLASS-004 / CLASS-005 are the buffered-path integration-transparency findings; report-writer/qa-bundler decides on bundling.
CLASS-006 is the carry-forward CurveAMMAdapter setRoute validation gap, first surfaced via convergent slither+aderyn+profiler+code-scanner signals this run.
No upstream ledger label changes required. L-01 remains the slippage-cap entry (mitigation overlap with CLASS-001 documented but L-01 root cause unchanged); C-01 envelope unchanged.
All six classifications are anchored to C4 severity criteria as written in project CLAUDE.md.
